name: Psychic Whorl
description: Target player discards two cards. If you control a Rat, you mill two cards. Scry 1.
assumptions: Read node D's `cond:you_control=rat` as "you control a Rat" (a creature with the Rat subtype in general), since the condition is free text rather than a reference to the `rat-1` token specifically.

Read the `qty:0..2` + `cond:you_control=rat` pairing on D (no `may` flag) as an all-or-nothing conditional ("if [condition], mill two cards") rather than a player-chosen "up to two," since nothing marks the count as optional/chosen — the range only exists to express "2 if the condition holds, 0 if not."
Used standard Magic terminology ("discards," "mill," "scry") as the printed-text equivalents of the schema's move/source/emit actions, since the schema itself doesn't dictate wording.
Treated node B (self, stack→gy) as the sorcery's own ordinary post-resolution zone change, not printed text — it's the default fate of any resolved sorcery, not an effect the card states.
couldNotDerive: Rarity — explicitly withheld by the exercise.
Any supertype (e.g., Legendary) — not present in the self registry entry, so left off rather than guessed.
Whether the discard in node C is restricted in any way (e.g., "of their choice," random, etc.) beyond a plain "discards two cards" — `thing: any` gives no further qualifier.
notes: Real card: Psychic Whorl, {2}{B} Sorcery — "Target player discards two cards. Then if you control a Rat, surveil 2." (forge-model/data/psychic-whorl.txt: A:SP$ Discard | ValidTgts$ Player | NumCards$ 2 | Mode$ TgtChoose | SubAbility$ DBSurveil; SVar:DBSurveil:DB$ Surveil | Amount$ 2 | ConditionPresent$ Rat.YouCtrl | ConditionCompare$ GE1.) This is the follow-up check after renaming node D's flag from `if_present=rat` to `you_control=rat` specifically to remove the board-state-vs-discard-byproduct ambiguity the previous (third) attempt fell into. PRIMARY FINDING, and the point of this exam: the rename worked. The examiner reconstructed `cond:you_control=rat` as "If you control a Rat," gating the clause on the caster's own battlefield state, with no trace of the prior wrong reading ("a Rat card was discarded/present among what C just discarded"). Its own assumption list confirms this explicitly — "you control a Rat (a creature with the Rat subtype in general)" — never referencing node C's discard output as the condition's scope. That is exactly the real card's meaning (`Rat.YouCtrl`, a permanent on the battlefield) and the only correct reading. The flag rename resolved the ambiguity: `you_control=X` was read correctly as a board-state check this time. SEPARATE, NEW issue, unrelated to the flag under test: nodes D+E were reconstructed as two distinct abilities ("you mill two cards. Scry 1.") instead of the single "surveil 2" they actually encode. D (`source`, owner `me`, `--`→`gy`, `qty:0..2`) followed by E (`emit`, `library-look`) is structurally identical to registries.json's own `surveil-N` template (a source with a `qty:0..N` range to `gy`, paired with an `emit library-look`), with N=2 — and that template was directly present in the packet the examiner read. `mill-N`'s registry entry, by contrast, uses a *fixed* `qty:N` with no range, which does not match D's `qty:0..2`. The examiner's own assumption text shows it explicitly considered the 0..2 range and interpreted it as an all-or-nothing toggle ("2 if condition, 0 if not") rather than recognizing the range as surveil's own discretionary count-to-graveyard shape — so this is agent misinterpretation, not a decomposition gap (D/E's edges are the same ones the successful namazu-trader-style surveil reconstructions parsed correctly) and not a schema gap (the disambiguating template was available and unambiguous). Net effect: "mill two cards. Scry 1" is not equivalent to "surveil 2" (mill forces both cards to the graveyard with no choice or reordering; scry 1 only inspects one card, not two), a genuine semantic miss — hence verdict issues-open rather than match. But scoped narrowly: the specific defect this exam was built to catch (misreading a board-state flag as being about an earlier effect's cards) did not recur.
